newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-New arrivals seen weighing down prices.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-New arrivals seen weighing down prices.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to slide this week in anticipation of new arrivals of fresh supplies in Rotterdam from Manila and Jakarta in the coming days, vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"Rotterdam will be swimming with a lot of oil starting on July 16 with the scheduled arrival of four ships carrying 100,000 tonnes," said a senior Manila trader.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam increased to 13,229 tonnes on June 17 from the previous week's 10,223.
But one trader said the market may break for a brief technical correction midweek. "It seemed like the market has reached its bottom at $625 per tonne CIF," he said.
Coconut oil buyers quoted $635 per tonne CIF for May/June shipment on Monday and $626.25 for September/October, trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines said.

The trader said prospects of a seasonal slowdown in Indonesian coconut oil exports in the third quarter might give the market an excuse to mount a technical rally. Indonesia has exported an average of 30,000 tonnes of coconut oil a month since the start of the year, he said.

Domestic coconut oil prices in the Philippines also picked up in recent days due to lack of supplies, the trader said, adding increased exports in the past few days might have temporarily dried up local supplies. --Manila newsroom (63 2) 841-8936, Fax 817-6267
